The mix of outcomes over time, with simultaneous intervals and trend tests

Source: R/justice.R
dispmix.Rd

For a table of counts – periods in rows, outcomes in columns, such as cases withdrawn, pleaded guilty, or tried – gives each outcome's share of its period with Goodman's simultaneous confidence intervals, tests whether the mix is the same in every period, and tests each outcome for a linear trend in its share.

Usage

dispmix(cnts, prd = NULL, scores = NULL, conflvl = 0.95)

Arguments

cnts

A matrix or data frame of non-negative counts, one row per period and one column per outcome. Columns that are not numeric are refused; pass only the outcome columns.

prd

Optional period labels (default: the row names, or 1:nrow(counts)).

scores

Numeric scores for the periods in the trend tests. Default: 1:nrow(counts), i.e. equally spaced.

conflvl

Confidence level. Default 0.95.

Value

A list of class rmbl_disposition_mix: shares, a long data frame (period, outcome, count, total, share, lower, upper); homogeneity, the Pearson chi-square test that every period has the same mix (with Cramer's V); trend, one row per outcome with the Cochran-Armitage trend statistic, its p-value, the Holm-adjusted p-value, and the change in share from the first to the last period.

Details

Goodman's intervals hold for all \(k\) shares of a period at once: with \(A\) the upper \(\alpha/k\) point of the chi-square distribution on one degree of freedom, the limits for a share \(n_i / N\) are $$\frac{A + 2 n_i \pm \sqrt{A (A + 4 n_i (N - n_i) / N)}}{2 (N + A)}.$$

The trend test for each outcome is the Cochran-Armitage test of its count against the period totals (stats::prop.trend.test()); the Holm adjustment covers the \(k\) tests. Counts of court cases are large, so these tests detect small changes; the shares and their intervals show whether a change is large enough to matter.

Errors: cnts not a numeric matrix or data frame, with a non-numeric column, fewer than one period or two outcomes, or a negative, missing or infinite count; a period with no cases; scores not one finite number per period, or all equal; prd of the wrong length or with repeats; conflvl outside (0, 1).

References

Goodman, L. A. (1965). On simultaneous confidence intervals for multinomial proportions. Technometrics, 7(2), 247-254.

Armitage, P. (1955). Tests for linear trends in proportions and frequencies. Biometrics, 11(3), 375-386.

Holm, S. (1979). A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 6(2), 65-70.

See also

shrs for one period's shares with Wilson intervals.

Examples

d <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "ocj_dispositions.csv",
                          package = "rmoriebricklayer"))
mix <- dispmix(d[, -(1:2)], prd = d$year)
mix
#> ── Outcome shares by period (95% Goodman simultaneous intervals in $shares)  
#>   Same mix in every period: chi-square 43792.1 on 66 df, p <2e-16, Cramer's V 0.052
#> 
#>                        outcome   2012   2013   2014   2015   2016   2017   2018
#>  withdrawn_stayed_before_trial 0.3796 0.3922 0.3980 0.4016 0.4093 0.4270 0.4411
#>       guilty_plea_before_trial 0.4236 0.4146 0.4094 0.4191 0.4199 0.4107 0.3999
#>             other_before_trial 0.0361 0.0349 0.0358 0.0364 0.0371 0.0377 0.0435
#>             withdrawn_at_trial 0.0554 0.0549 0.0547 0.0482 0.0452 0.0421 0.0386
#>           guilty_plea_at_trial 0.0536 0.0521 0.0499 0.0462 0.0426 0.0388 0.0366
#>                 other_at_trial 0.0012 0.0011 0.0012 0.0010 0.0009 0.0007 0.0006
#>                following_trial 0.0506 0.0502 0.0510 0.0475 0.0450 0.0430 0.0397
#>    2019   2021   2022   2024   2025
#>  0.4365 0.5326 0.5429 0.5180 0.5088

plot(mix)
